correctness.rationale: The explicit bilinear cocycle has square Q(x) with edge coordinates x_i x_j and commutator C_x(y) with edge coordinates x_i y_j+x_j y_i. Square-zero is equivalent to independent coordinate support. For independent support S, C_x has field rank exactly |N(S)| by disjoint edge-coordinate blocks for distinct exterior neighbors, establishing order-conditioned conjugacy sizes. Every elementary abelian subgroup H extends by the central elementary abelian W; above W its quotient U is an F2-subspace all of whose squares vanish. A pair of nonzero edge-coordinate projections cannot simultaneously have disjoint nonzero support throughout U, because two proper kernels cannot cover U. Therefore support(U) is independent. Inclusion-exclusion gives every subgroup rank; maximality gives H_S for maximal independent S. The argument covers disconnected and edgeless graphs and every q=2^e. The included verifier exhaustively corroborates 84 graph-field configurations.

value.rationale: Order-two elements, conjugacy-class sizes, and maximal elementary abelian subgroups are canonical structural invariants in finite group theory. This exact complete correspondence for all finite graphs and characteristic-two extensions identifies the graph independence polynomial in the group involution count, open-neighborhood statistics in the involution conjugacy profile, maximal independent sets in the full maximal elementary abelian subgroup classification, and well-coveredness in equicardinality of maximal subgroups. The binary Gaussian transform counts every subgroup rank above the natural central edge subgroup. This is structurally motivated rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
